name: Jonnah
title: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
summary: Jonam is a person mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke. He is the son of Eliakim and the father of Joseph (not Mary's husband, but another Joseph in the lineage). Little is known about his life beyond his place in the family register that connects Jesus to King David and further back to Adam.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus
keyEvents.description: Jonam is listed in Luke's genealogy of Jesus Christ, as part of the line from David through Nathan. He is placed between Eliakim (his father) and Joseph (his son).

keyEvents.title: Part of David's royal line
keyEvents.description: Through his place in the genealogy, Jonam is part of the messianic line that stretches from King David to Jesus Christ, through David's son Nathan.

keyEvents.title: Connection to God's plan of salvation
keyEvents.description: As a link in the genealogy of Jesus, Jonam testifies to God's faithfulness across generations in fulfilling the promise of a Messiah from the house of David.

keyEvents.title: The Promise of David's Eternal Throne
keyEvents.description: Jonah's place in the genealogy points back to God's covenant with David that his throne would endure forever, a promise fulfilled in Jesus Christ.
